boundaries: The fix is CLI composition validation only; ticket IDs, transaction IDs, ledger schema, execution engine, fixtures, wire protocol, and authorization rules were not changed.
Legacy --execute-wave without a ticket mutation remains supported. The rejected case is its combination with Mint, Transfer, or Revoke in one invocation.
Hashes and transaction identifiers are not signatures, witnesses, ZK proofs, publisher authentication, or remote-attestation evidence.

The evidence covers local CLI composition, snapshot history, recovery, and replay behavior in the executed fixtures; it does not establish distributed exactly-once, hostile-OS or hostile-writer safety, cross-host locking, WAL/fsync durability, consensus, external settlement, CI, federation ACK, or production-scale agent validation.
